I've been farming this same land for 25 years. My plot is small — 3.5 mu — and with my son and daughter-in-law working in the city, the farm mostly falls to me. I grow maize. That's what I know, and that's what sells locally.

I plant summer maize every year, after the spring frosts are gone, around late May or early June. I use hybrid seed — I stopped using saved seed a long time ago because the yields just aren't as good. Everyone in the village buys hybrid now. I'll buy the same variety I used last year from the seed shop in town since it did well.

For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer (复合肥) at planting, then come back with urea when the plants are knee-high at the jointing stage. I've been doing it this way for years. I probably apply around 18 jin of pure nitrogen per mu total — maybe a bit more, my son says I overdo it but the plants look healthy.

I have a well, so I can water when I need to. I'll irrigate at planting if the soil is dry, again at jointing, and again around silking time — that's when the plant really needs water. Three times usually is enough, sometimes two if it rains well.

I spray herbicide right after planting — once. I also spray for corn borer (玉米螟) once in midsummer. That's usually enough unless there's a bad pest year.

For tillage, I hire a rotary tiller — it's cheap to hire and breaks up the soil well. I can't manage deep ploughing alone.

I expect around 550 kg per mu. Some years it's more, some less. It's reliable enough.
